tagline: Off the Blue Ridge from Meadows of Dan toward Stuart.
intro: US 58 crosses the Blue Ridge Parkway at Meadows of Dan and winds its way toward Stuart, past the hamlet of Vesta, seven and a half miles out of town. The byway stops at Route 8, just north of Stuart. Its predecessor here was the Danville and Wytheville Turnpike of the 1850s.
The highway carries the name of J.E.B. Stuart, and so does the county seat it is headed for, which started out as Taylorsville.

moments.title: Meadows of Dan
moments.text: A crossroads of country shops at Parkway milepost 178, named for the meadows along the Dan, where a Mayberry Road is one guess at where the television town got its name.

moments.title: Mabry Mill
moments.text: Just up the Parkway, E. B. Mabry's mill was a blacksmith and wheelwright shop when he started building in 1903, and grinding as a gristmill by 1905.
